$comment: R1770 — `$at` is the SURFACE EXTENT this canon was written against, and it
is load-bearing here rather than merely informative: the `theme` entry in
`rows` below is a FOLD, and a fold is a function of how tall the surface
is. At 2494x1531 the row fits, the difference is gone, and a ledger with
no size reported that entry paid and demanded its deletion — which would
have broken this same tool at 1440x900. The entry now names its extent.
R1762 — THE PREFERENCES SECTION'S PAINTED SURFACES, written down from the
behaviour reference in neutral vocabulary, so the last unjudged section of
the assembled application can be judged against something other than its
own tables.
WHY THIS PIN COULD NOT BE WRITTEN AT R1761. The mechanism to publish a
verdict for a page the host paints landed then (`SectionJudge`), and this
entry stayed open anyway, because a pin that specified only what the build
already drew would be a document that cannot fail — R1747's defect made on
purpose. Measured at R1761 against the reference: this build's preferences
page was MISSING three of the reference's ten rows (a capture-source row
and a retention row in the first group, a payload-format row in the
second), had neither the page heading the reference opens with nor the
build strip it closes with, and its four group headings were loose ink no
specification could address. R1762 built all of it first; this file is
what became writable afterwards.
THE TEN ROWS ARE THE REFERENCE'S TEN. That is the surface worth having:
the reference's page is a list of rows in four groups, and `rows` below is
that list, in that order, read back out of the frame. A row missing, a row
renamed, or a row that moved between groups all read as a difference here.
HOW A PART IS TITLED, AND WHY IT DIFFERS PER SURFACE. Where the reference
fixes the WORDS a reader reads — the page's heading, a group's heading, a
row's title and the sentence under it, a booked row's verb, the appearance
choices, the payload formats — the title here is those words and the judge
reads them back off the frame. Where a part is a VALUE a session changes
(which capture source is in effect, which buffer size) or a control that
draws no words at all (a switch is a track and a knob), the title is this
screen's own name for it and what the pin fixes is the roster and its
order. `crate::judge` says which is which per surface and why.
WHAT IS THE REFERENCE'S AND WHAT IS THIS BUILD'S. Every row, every heading
and every group is the reference's. Three things are not, and all three are
recorded as remainders below rather than written in as if they were: the
two rows whose values are this tool's own vocabulary, and the payload
formats, which the reference names as two third-party serialisations and
this build names for what they are.

owed.sentence: part 9 `theme` (Theme Both themes are first-class) is specified and the surface has no such part
owed.why: The last row of ten, and the page scrolls — exactly as the reference's does. The page's content is 946 pixels tall in a region of 820, so at the OPENING scroll position the appearance group is not on the frame; scrolling to the foot puts it there, and this entry is what says that is the reason rather than a row this build does not draw. The alternative was an away-condition of `the page can not show all ten rows at once`, refused for R1742's reason: it would swallow a page that had genuinely stopped drawing a row. R1770 — a fold is a function of how tall the surface is, so this entry names the extent it was read at; at 2494x1531 the whole page fits, the difference is gone, and the ledger reports this entry PAID, which is why the extent list is not a band. ★★★★★ R1864 REWROTE THE SENTENCE AND NEARLY DELETED THE ENTRY, AND THE SECOND WOULD HAVE BEEN WRONG. The sentence changed because the host reserved a status band: the group used to STRADDLE the fold, so the row's title painted and the line under it did not (`reads "Theme"`); with 28 pixels less region it is wholly below the fold and the part is absent. The deletion was proposed because the walk's FOLDED verdict — R1864 taught the preferences page to declare two frames and taught `SurfaceStanding::folded_with` to credit a part either frame had — reported this entry PAID on the second frame. It is not paid: `tools/demos/r1762_the_last_unjudged_section_answers.py` drives the RUNNING binary at its opening frame and failed the moment the entry was removed, exactly as the sentence this note replaces had predicted in as many words. ⇒ A LEDGER ENTRY IS A CLAIM ABOUT A FRAME AND A WALK'S VERDICT IS A CLAIM ABOUT A SECTION, and a folded verdict must never be used to retire a per-frame entry. What keeps the two from contradicting each other is that the fold INTERSECTS unreconciled claims: this entry is matched at the first frame and unpaid at the second, so it survives in neither the walk's verdict nor a single frame's — and it is a demo driving the real binary that says which of those is the one a reader meets.

owed.sentence: part 0 `0` (Dark) is specified and the surface has no such part
owed.why: The appearance group is the last of four on a page whose content is 946 pixels tall in a region of 820, so at the OPENING scroll position it is not on the frame at all — and these two controls are inside it. ★★★★★ THIS ENTRY IS THE PRICE OF THE STATUS BAND, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. Before R1864 the page had 848 pixels of region and the same group STRADDLED the fold: a node partly outside a viewport is still painted, so these two controls were on the frame and this surface owed nothing. Reserving 28 pixels of host furniture along the window's bottom moved the group from partly visible to outside, and a reader arriving at the preferences page now sees the `Appearance` heading with nothing under it until they scroll. That is a real cost and it belongs in the ledger, not in a gap tuned until the number came out right — tuning a layout constant to hide a shortfall is the defect R1864 spent its round removing from two other places on this screen. The page is REACHABLE in full: `pinion_screen::SectionPoser` gives it a second frame, `SurfaceStanding::folded_with` credits a part either frame had, and the walk this application publishes at `/external/journey` reports the section reproduced. `tools/demos/r1762_the_last_unjudged_section_answers.py` asserts both halves — this entry against the frame a reader arrives on, and the walk against the page.
